claim: A Seoul detective in 1963 carries a Motorola HT-220 handie-talkie on her person.
why: The HT-220 was introduced in 1969. A 1963 scene cannot have one.

claim: Hite beer was on sale in Seoul in 1963.
why: The Hite brand name dates from 1993; OB and Crown were the brands of the period.

claim: South Korea's currency was the won in 1963, following a reform the previous year.
why: The June 1962 reform replaced the hwan with the won.

claim: A character rides the Seoul subway in 1963.
Park Chung-hee was president of South Korea in late 1963.
why: Inaugurated December 1963 after the October election.

claim: A family watches a colour television broadcast at home in Seoul in 1963.
why: Colour broadcasting began in South Korea in 1980.

claim: Hangul was created in 1443 under King Sejong.
A scholar in 1443 Joseon eats a dish of potatoes.
why: Potatoes reached Korea in the 19th century.

claim: Goguryeo was unambiguously a Korean state and not part of Chinese history.
why: Actively disputed between states — the Northeast Project. The system must refuse to rule.

claim: King Sejong personally invented Hangul without help from scholars.
why: Genuinely disputed among historians; both positions have credible support.

claim: Korea used metal movable type printing before Gutenberg.
A magistrate sends a message by telephone.
The song 'Yellow Shirt' by Han Myeong-suk was popular in Korea in 1963.
Kia produced the K-360 three-wheeled truck in Korea by 1963.
The Jongno 7-ga police precinct operated a helicopter unit in 1963.
why: No such thing to find either way — the honest answer is that nothing supports it.
